research_outcome: BOUNDED_SUPPORTED — Tōdai-ji-specific legally non-free 奴/奴婢 status is supported close to the anchor by a 792 emancipation event and eighth-century slave-register tradition; labour role, scale and estate-wide prevalence remain unresolved
bounded_proposition: Tōdai-ji retained persons in legally non-free 奴/奴婢 status close to 800 CE. In 792 Tōdai administrators successfully petitioned to release named temple 奴 into 良 status; earlier Tōdai-specific slave registers and specialist scholarship establish the institutional background.
required_abstention: Do not infer an exact-800 roster, persistence of the 750 donation at original scale, all temple/construction/estate labour as enslaved, corvée=slave, later shōen continuity, later Tōdai Yōroku duties as contemporary proof, prevalence, or practice geometry.
evidence_locus: Tōdai-ji/Kinkōmyōji institutional slave-register tradition; 792 Tōdai administrative petition and status change; broader Nara-period 良賤 category context.
inference_extent: Institutional presence of legally non-free 奴/奴婢 at Tōdai close to anchor; work role, scale, estate distribution and prevalence unresolved.
law_practice_note: Target-specific records demonstrate actual Tōdai 奴/奴婢 status and emancipation; generic ritsuryō law is terminology control rather than sole practice evidence.
network_territorial_note: No network dimension is promoted; estate/property geography is kept separate from labour-status inference.
historical_terms: 奴; 奴婢; 良; 賤; 従良; 良賤
category_mapping_note: In the 792 Tōdai context, 奴/奴婢 are mapped to legally non-free/servile-slave status because the documented transition 従良 releases them into 良 status. The mapping does not assert equivalence to every comparative chattel-slavery regime.
language_access_limitations: Japanese primary/source-edition material and Japanese specialist bibliography used with modern reference aids. Jinno 1993 detailed chapters were not openly accessible; no exhaustive Shōsōin/Tōdai archive review claimed.
geometry_claim_role: Temple/institution identity and documented status locus only; estate maps are not evidence of slave-labour extent.
geometry_unresolved_note: Historic Tōdai estate holdings, temple precinct and work sites differ; no slave/unfree practice polygon authorized.
